title: Validate a pipeline definition
description: Validate a proposed autoresearch pipeline before creating it. The target is either an event (pass target_event) or a PostHog action (pass target_definition = {"type": "action", "action_id": N}); base-rate and volume estimates are computed against whichever you provide. Returns volume estimates, base rate, positive and negative example counts, and a list of warnings. Check 'can_proceed' before calling autoresearch-create: if false, resolve errors first. 'requires_acknowledgement' means there are non-blocking warnings worth noting. Errors (can_proceed is false): low_volume (fewer than 100 users), low_positives or low_negatives (fewer than 20 examples), horizon_exceeds_lookback (raise training_lookback_days above horizon_days), and population_too_large with severity error (narrow the training population). Non-blocking warnings include extreme_imbalance (base rate below 1%) and near_universal (above 95%). population_too_large with severity info means the inference population is above the cap, so each scoring run scores users never scored first, then those scored longest ago. The warning message gives how many scoring runs it takes to rescore everyone (ceil(eligible / 45000)), which in days is that many times the pipeline's cadence_days. An action target needs the action:read scope. Always validate before creating.

methodDocumentation.text: Validate a proposed pipeline's target event and population before creating it. Returns volume estimates, base rate, and any warnings. Creation does not enforce the result: 'horizon_exceeds_lookback' and an 'error' 'population_too_large' mean a run would fail, and the other 'error' codes mean the data is too thin for a reliable model. Call this before autoresearch-create.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription: Machine-readable warning code. 'horizon_exceeds_lookback', and 'population_too_large' with severity 'error', mean a run would fail: fix the definition before creating. 'population_too_large' with severity 'info' means training uses a sample of the population, or each scoring run scores a rolling part of it: users never scored first, then users whose last score was oldest. 'low_volume', 'low_positives' and 'low_negatives' mean the data is too thin for a reliable model (severity 'error', advisory). 'moderate_volume', 'mostly_anonymous_population', 'extreme_imbalance' and 'near_universal' are severity 'warning'.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription:
Severity level. 'error' means training would fail or the data is too thin for a reliable model; see 'code' for which. 'warning' is worth acknowledging. Creation enforces none of them.

* `info` - info
* `warning` - warning
* `error` - error
